O.outcome_detail: language or literacy performance in six possible domains

cells.quote: Of the 132 interventions evaluated by high-quality impact studies, 38 demonstrated effectiveness in at least one language or literacy outcome domain relative to the comparison group. All other studied interventions except one (93 of 132) demonstrated inconclusive effects.
cells.note: The review synthesized experimental and quasi-experimental studies; the text reports intervention-level effectiveness counts rather than one pooled effect size.

cells.quote: Among interventions that taught language exclusively, interventions classified as instructional practices produced a significantly larger weighted effect size on language performance than interventions classified as curricula (0.43 versus 0.02; see table B6 in appendix B).
cells.note: The weighted effects were calculated across interventions in the systematic review.

D.treatment: language instruction with one-on-one or small-group implementation
D.comparison: language instruction exclusively in large-group or whole-class configurations

cells.quote: The weighted effect size on language performance was significantly larger when language instruction included some one-on-one or small-group implementation than when it used large-group or whole-class configurations exclusively (0.43 versus 0.10; figure 2). Furthermore, interventions that used large-group or whole-class configurations exclusively did not improve language performance relative to the comparison group.
cells.note: The implementation characteristics were analyzed across the language-exclusive interventions for which sufficient information was available.

D.treatment: instruction teaching a specific language or literacy domain

O.outcome_detail: performance in the taught domain; some evidence for print knowledge, decoding, and early writing from combined phonological-awareness and print-knowledge instruction

cells.quote: The findings revealed that instruction that teaches a specific domain is likely to increase performance in that domain. Interventions that teach language exclusively might be more beneficial when conducted in small groups or one-on-one than in larger group sizes. In addition, teaching both phonological awareness and print knowledge might benefit performance in print knowledge. Finally, some evidence indicates that instruction that teaches both phonological awareness and print knowledge might also lead to improvements in decoding and early writing performance.
cells.note: The summary reports these as review-level findings without a single printed effect size for the domain combinations.

D.treatment: online simulation studies with learner diversity as a main focus
D.comparison: studies that mentioned learner diversity briefly or did not plan for it

O.outcome_detail: attention to and planned response to learner diversity

cells.quote: Five studies embedded learner diversity as a main focus in the aims and objectives. ... The findings show that few studies planned for learner diversity in their aims or objectives, while the majority briefly mention the significance of this concept indicating a lack of response to learner diversity.
cells.note: Narrative scoping-review synthesis; the review did not report a quantitative comparative effect.

D.treatment: EDI theory or framework guiding online simulation
D.comparison: non-EDI educational or simulation framework, or no framework

O.outcome_detail: adoption of an EDI framework in online simulation design

cells.quote: Whilst no study specifically utilized an EDI theory/framework, the majority of studies indicate that online SBL approaches are underpinned by educational theoretical frameworks and best practice standards, as outlined in Table 4.
cells.note: The review found no explicit use of an EDI theory/framework; this is a descriptive synthesis rather than a controlled comparison.

D.treatment: inclusive pedagogy addressed in online simulation literature
D.comparison: inclusive pedagogy not defined or explicitly addressed

cells.quote: No primary study or review defined, or made explicit reference to the concept of inclusive pedagogy, therefore it could be argued that no study met the research question. ... Inclusive pedagogy has not been considered or embedded in its entirety in online simulation in undergraduate nursing education literature.
cells.note: This codes the review's overall conclusion; no experimental treatment effect was reported.
